title: Cartesian exchange of a single compactification graph comparison
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, and $(v,f\prime,f,b)$ a Cartesian square from $f\prime:X\prime\to Y\prime$ to $f:X\to Y$. Let $c,d$ be compactifications of $f$, and $d\prime$ one of $f\prime$, with a map $w:d\prime.Z\to d.Z$ such that the squares of the open parts $(v,d\prime.i,d.i,w)$ and proper parts $(w,d\prime.g,d.g,b)$ are Cartesian. Write $G(c,d)$ for the specified graph comparison [def-asd-open-restriction-comparisons], and $Q(d,d\prime)$ for the raw proper-exchange/inverse-open-exchange map for these representatives. Then $(G(c,d)b^*);Q(d,d\prime)=B(c);(v^*G(c\times_Y Y\prime,d\prime))$, where $B$ is the literal compactification exchange [def-asd-open-restriction-comparisons]. This concerns only the graph factor; no open restriction of the bases is present. No quasi-compactness is assumed.

source.place: Coherence (i): compare the proper/open diagram with its base change; the open factors are handled by the adjunction transposition in coherence (iii).

proof.text: Identify the explicit graph comparison with etaleGraphComparisonFromOpen followed by the open normalization removing R(id)_*. Apply the general single-graph exchange to the presentation of d and its supplied Cartesian representative d\prime.

Remove the identity proper factor using its unit-normalized exchange equation; paste with the graph equation. Translate the exact inverse image exchanges to left derived inverse image through the canonical natural isomorphisms. Naturality and cancellation of these isomorphisms give the displayed equation.
